items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: And my brother, Charles, was a great help with us, although he didn't share in the gravy of the band.

ctx.x: Yeah. Well, Jeta -- I tell you, we got along this way. He took care of all the business of the band, paid the guys off. I was in charge of the music end of the band. If I saw a musician I thought the band -- was good enough for the band, I picked him out and tell everybody, I think we should get this guy, get that guy. I did the recruiting. And a lot of times we would have a few arguments. And things just weren't rosy all the time.

But I understood him and I think he understood me, see. And my brother, Charles, was a great help with us, although he didn't share in the gravy of the band. There was very little gravy for the band, you see. But there were times when we would give him a little extra or something here or something there, see.

But I really wish it had been so we should have done -- and frankly speaking, I really feel that the two of us for him, could have done more A being honest about it. And he stuck with us right through. That's why I feel --
